1 حَرَى , aor. يَحْرِى, (S, K,) inf. n. حَرْىٌ, (S,) It (a thing S) decreased, diminished, or waned, (S, K, TA,) after increase; (TA;) as does, for instance, the moon. (S, TA.) [See an ex. in a verse cited in art. است.] ＝
-A2- حَرَى أَنْ يَكُونَ ذٰلِكَ i. q. عَسَى [May-be, or may-hap, &c., that will be]. (TA.) ＝
-A3- حَرِىَ بِكَذَا He was, or became, adapted, disposed, apt, meet, suited, suitable, fitted, fit, competent, or proper, for such a thing; or worthy of it. (MA.) ＝
-A4- حَرَاهُ: see 5.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
